state.requirement: PackJoyU M5-T1 supplies JobState atomic claim, renewal and guarded completion primitives. Repository operations reuse a service-owned Prisma transaction. Completion must verify owner, generation, unexpired lease and current timezone revision, and business results must roll back with rejected completion. The documented M5-T3 consumer uses RepeatableRead. SiteSetting analytics.settings has a documented initial UTC timezone and revision 1, initialized idempotently; no production deployment is authorized.

task.title: M5-T1 review round 2: finish R1-R4 without a third rework cycle
task.accept: Real PostgreSQL 17 concurrency and rollback tests with zero environment skips; old workers and old timezone revisions cannot commit. Only the existing lease repository, types, schema, deploy hook and lease test paths are in production scope.

state.conflict: The submitted repair takes a SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE table lock and SELECT FOR UPDATE on analytics.settings. In an outer RepeatableRead transaction that established its snapshot while the row was absent, another connection can commit revision 2 before the table lock is taken. The later SELECT still sees no row and defaults to revision 1, so the old revision can commit despite the lock. The reviewer must repair this concrete R3 residue within the existing scope. R1 will separately remove all repository-owned transaction fallbacks and require a caller transaction for renew/complete.

options.A: Keep guarded completion composable with the caller transaction. When the locked settings lookup is empty, materialize the documented initial UTC/revision1 value using parameterized INSERT ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE returning the existing value unchanged. A row inserted after a RepeatableRead snapshot then causes PostgreSQL serialization failure and the whole outer transaction rolls back. Normal ReadCommitted missing-row completion continues to work. Preserve valid existing settings; add real RepeatableRead race and rollback regression tests.
options.B: Initialize the documented settings singleton idempotently as part of claim before returning a lease, so subsequent worker snapshots contain a durable row. Completion must fail closed if the settings row is absent rather than infer revision1 from an empty old snapshot. Keep row locking and add RepeatableRead and missing-row regressions. This adds a settings initialization side effect to claim.
options.C: Avoid creating settings in the lease primitive. Keep existing ReadCommitted missing-row serialization, but explicitly reject completion when the caller uses RepeatableRead and the settings row is absent. Let the documented settings initialization service create the row before aggregate execution. Add tests proving rejection rolls back business results; document that precondition without relaxing owner/generation/revision safety.
